status.en: 221 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Plateau State.
status.nb: 221 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Plateau State.

summary.en: Bandits continue to raid villages and block a deputy governor convoy in Zamfara while gunmen shot the Miyetti Allah chairman in Plateau and assaulted police stations in Plateau, Abia and Borno, killing several officers. ISWAP militants placed landmines on a highway in Borno that killed eight soldiers and later claimed an attack that killed 21 soldiers and militiamen at an army base. President Tinubu approved security equipment to protect trains from bandit attacks. An air traffic controller remains captive after being abducted at Sokoto airport for 52 days. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Bandittene fortsetter å raidere landsbyer og blokkerer en viseprefektkonvoi i Zamfara mens væpnede menn skjøt Miyetti Allah-lederen i Plateau og angrep politistasjoner i Plateau, Abia og Borno, og drepte flere offiserer. ISWAP-militante la landminer på en motorvei i Borno som drepte åtte soldater og hevdet senere et angrep som drepte 21 soldater og militsmedlemmer på en militærbase. President Tinubu godkjente sikkerhetsutstyr for å beskytte tog mot bandittangrep. En flykontrollør er fortsatt holdt fanget etter å ha blitt bortført på flyplassen i Sokoto i 52 dager. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
